title: As researchers age, they produce less disruptive work
summary: This article explores research findings showing that as scientists age, their work becomes less disruptive and innovative, supporting the provocative notion that 'science advances one funeral at a time'. Studies using citation analysis and disruption indices demonstrate that scientific breakthrough contributions decline significantly as researchers grow older.
problem_solved: Explains why scientific innovation is often driven by younger researchers and how age-related cognitive shifts affect breakthrough discoveries.
why_valuable: Provides empirical evidence for understanding how scientific paradigms shift, why younger researchers drive innovation, and the importance of nurturing new generations of scientists.
